body: The spec is on the whole disciplined, but the control-perturbation logic in FR-021/FR-022 does not establish what it claims. Permuting rows within each column preserves every marginal exactly while destroying all dependence structure; hence this dataset is a ground truth only for correlation fidelity (all pairs unfaithful) and, for marginals, is indistinguishable from the real hold-out (all columns faithful). It therefore cannot yield both false-positive and false-negative rates: against a reference whose labels are known only in one direction per metric family, one of the two error rates is undefined. FR-022 should be restricted to the correlation metrics, or a second control constructed (e.g., permuted marginals with preserved copula) to cover the other direction. Second, the categorical effect-size threshold in FR-020 is not an effect size: the chi-square statistic scales with sample size and degrees of freedom, so a fixed cutoff 'χ² ≤ χ²₀.₉₅' is either trivially violated or trivially satisfied depending on N and column cardinality; Cramér's V (or N-rescaled divergence) would be the commensurable quantity. Third, the assumption that 'power is assumed sufficient due to large N' cuts against the study: with N in the tens of thousands, KS and chi-square p-values will reject for negligible deviations, so the p-value leg of FR-020 will classify nearly everything unfaithful and the sensitivity sweep over {0.01, 0.05, 0.1} will show almost no variation — the effect-size leg is doing all the work, and the spec should say so. Finally, minor but real: FR-007 cites 'the control-perturbation dataset defined in FR-022' when the dataset is defined in FR-021, and FR-021 contains an unresolved placeholder ('randomly permuting [deferred] of rows') that leaves the perturbation fraction unspecified — a parameter that directly determines how unfaithful the control is, and hence the measured error rates.
